translations.idiomatic: Assaulting a blockhouse he was shot in the right thigh.

sentences.zh: 錄功，擢四川威茂協右營都司。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to battalion commander of the right camp of the Weimao garrison in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds were entered on the rolls and he was promoted to battalion commander of the Weimao right camp in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 引見，賜大緞。

translations.literal: Granted an audience, he was bestowed fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he was rewarded with fine silk.

sentences.zh: 雜穀土司蒼旺為亂，提督岳鍾琪檄進忠討之，奪銅砲一，斬馘數十，生擒二十五，降茶堡番民二千餘。

translations.literal: When the Zagu chieftain Cangwang rebelled, Provincial Commander Yue Zhongqi by dispatch ordered Jinzhong to suppress him; he seized one bronze cannon, killed and wounded several tens, captured twenty-five alive, and received the surrender of more than two thousand Chabao tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangwang of Zagu rebelled, Yue Zhongqi dispatched Jinzhong to suppress him; he took one bronze cannon, killed or wounded several dozen, captured twenty-five alive, and received the submission of more than two thousand Chabao tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 自角木角溝入雜穀，獲蒼旺。

translations.literal: Entering Zagu from Jiaomujiao Ravine, he captured Cangwang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zagu from Jiaomujiao Ravine and captured Cangwang.

sentences.zh: 累擢永寧協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to brigade deputy commander of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to brigade deputy commander of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 三十年，從將軍明瑞徵緬甸，進攻蠻結，克木卡十六，殪賊三，傷額，明日，仍裹創出戰。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he followed General Ming Rui in the Burma campaign, advanced to attack Manjie, captured sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and the next day still went out to fight wrapped in bandages.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty he followed General Ming Rui against Burma, attacked Manjie, took sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and fought again the next day still bandaged.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜孔雀翎，號法式善巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When this was reported he was granted a peacock feather and given the title Fashishan Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court he received a peacock feather and the title Fashishan Batulu.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南臨元鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional commander of Linyuan in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander of Linyuan in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 明瑞令將五千人屯龍陵關備調遣。

translations.literal: Ming Rui ordered him to station five thousand men at Longling Pass for deployment as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui stationed him with five thousand men at Longling Pass for deployment as needed.

sentences.zh: 召詣熱河行在，入見，命乾清門行走，賜貂皮、銀幣，令還軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe, granted an audience, ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and bestowed sable fur and silver coins, then ordered back to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Rehe traveling palace, he was granted audience, assigned to the Gate of Heavenly Purity, rewarded with sable and silver, and sent back to the army.

sentences.zh: 旋移普洱鎮總兵，擢雲南提督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Pu'er and promoted to provincial military commander of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Pu'er as regional commander and promoted to provincial commander of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 卒，加太子太保，諡勤毅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Qinyi (Diligent and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 劉順，順天人。

translations.literal: Liu Shun was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shun was from Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: A military jinshi in the fifth year of Yongzheng, he was appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather.
translations.idiomatic: He took the military jinshi in Yongzheng 5 (1727) and was made an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather.

sentences.zh: 以守備發陝西。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to Shaanxi as a garrison commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Shaanxi as a garrison commandant.

sentences.zh: 累遷至金塔協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to brigade deputy commander of Jinta.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to brigade deputy commander of Jinta.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，令將千五百人赴金川，偕副將高雄自甲索攻囊得，道松林。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he was ordered to lead fifteen hundred men to Jinchuan; together with Brigade Deputy Gao Xiong he attacked Nangde from Jiasuo by way of the pine forest.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 he was ordered to Jinchuan with fifteen hundred men; with Brigade Deputy Gao Xiong he attacked Nangde from Jiasuo through the pine woods.

sentences.zh: 賊百餘出戰，擊之遁，毀賊碉。

translations.literal: More than a hundred rebels came out to fight; he attacked and drove them off and destroyed rebel blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a hundred rebels sallied out he beat them back and destroyed their blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 從大軍自卡撒左山梁進，諸碉以次皆下。

translations.literal: Following the main army he advanced from the left ridge of Kasai, and the blockhouses fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: With the main army he advanced from Kasai's left ridge and the blockhouses fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 惟普瞻雙、單二碉守甚堅。

translations.literal: Only the paired and single blockhouses at Puzhan were defended with especial firmness.
translations.idiomatic: Only the twin and single blockhouses at Puzhan held out with special stubbornness.

sentences.zh: 日暮，將收兵，順潛率所部逼單碉，縱火攻之，賊潰，並奪雙碉。

translations.literal: At dusk, as the army was about to withdraw, Shun secretly led his detachment against the single blockhouse, set fire to attack it, the rebels were routed, and he also seized the paired blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, as the army was pulling back, Shun secretly led his men against the single blockhouse, fired it, routed the defenders, and seized the paired blockhouses as well.

sentences.zh: 師繼進，遂克色底。

translations.literal: The army pressed on and then captured Sedi.
translations.idiomatic: The main force followed up and took Sedi.

sentences.zh: 普瞻西有山曰阿利，賊碉林立。

translations.literal: West of Puzhan was a mountain called Ali, with blockhouses standing in dense array.
translations.idiomatic: West of Puzhan stood Mount Ali, its slopes thick with blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 順冒雨奮攻，奪山樑木卡，破碉。

translations.literal: Shun attacked fiercely in the rain, seized the ridge palisade, and broke the blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: Shun attacked through the rain, took the ridge palisade, and stormed the blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 發砲，殪賊數十，复破大碉一、石卡四。

translations.literal: He fired cannon and killed several tens of rebels, and again broke one great blockhouse and four stone palisades.
translations.idiomatic: He shelled the position, killed several dozen rebels, and took one great blockhouse and four stone palisades.

sentences.zh: 經略訥親屢奏順奮勇。

translations.literal: Commissioner-General Neqin repeatedly memorialized that Shun fought with valor.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner-General Neqin repeatedly reported Shun's valor in battle.

sentences.zh: 金川平，擢貴州威寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified he was promoted to regional commander of Weining in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified he was promoted to regional commander of Weining in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 上以順熟邊情，移甘肅西寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew Shun was familiar with frontier conditions, he was transferred to regional commander of Xining in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Shun's knowledge of the frontier, the emperor transferred him to regional commander of Xining in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 入見，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Granted an audience, he was given a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 擢安西提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial military commander of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial commander of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 病，乞罷。

translations.literal: He fell ill and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，加太子太保，諡壯靖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhuangjing (Stalwart and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 論曰：初徵金川，攀龍、舉、大雄皆以勇略著。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the first campaign against Jinchuan, Panlong, Ju, and Daxiong were all noted for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: In the first Jinchuan campaign Panlong, Ju, and Daxiong all won fame for courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 舉尤驍桀為軍鋒，訥親、張廣泗督戰急，鼓銳攻堅，遂以身殉，傷已！

translations.literal: Ju was especially fierce and served as the army's spearhead; Neqin and Zhang Guangsi pressed the campaign urgently, rousing sharp attacks on strong positions, and so he died for the cause — a grievous loss!
translations.idiomatic: Ju was the fiercest, the army's spearhead; Neqin and Zhang Guangsi drove the war hard, urging assaults on the strongest points, and so he died in service — a grievous loss!

sentences.zh: 良柱善戰，又以廣泗牽制，不能盡其材。

translations.literal: Liangzhu was skilled in battle, yet because Guangsi held him back he could not fully deploy his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhu fought well, yet Zhang Guangsi's obstruction kept him from giving his full measure.

sentences.zh: 進忠、順力戰破堅碉，亦攀龍輩之亞也。

translations.literal: Jinzhong and Shun fought hard to break stubborn blockhouses; they rank just below Panlong and his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong and Shun fought through the hardest blockhouses; they stand just below men like Panlong.
